messages.subject: using mlm estimator in EFA
parts:
Hi!
Thank you for the help, first off!
I'm running an EFA on a new measure, and even though skew and kurtosis are under 2 for all items, some kurtosi are pretty close to 2. I wanted to run EFA using a robust ML estimator, but I cant seem to figure out how to use the lavaan package's mlm estimator for the EFA.
Any help is appreciated, thanks a lot!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: using mlm estimator in EFA
parts: I wanted to run EFA using a robust ML estimator, but I cant seem to figure out how to use the lavaan package's mlm estimator for the EFA.

The lavaan package itself is only equipped for CFA, but you can still specify them as the EFA models you want to investigate (testing models with increasing numbers of factors).  The semTools package has a couple of functions that have automated the process so that you only have to specify the variable names and the number of factors you want, and then rotate the fitted solution.  Check out these help pages:

library(semTools)
?efaUnrotate
?oblqRotate

Terry
